summary: This entry synthesizes foundational work in memory management, RAGAS-based evaluation, and performance monitoring. By merging semantic caching, loop detection, and sys.monitoring, the system establishes a robust, low-overhead framework for tracking architectural evolution and ensuring progress remains monotonic.
key_learnings: Memory compression is best measured via task-agnostic evaluation like RAGAS.
Event-based monitoring (sys.monitoring) provides higher precision and lower overhead than traditional sampling.
Semantic Loop Detection serves as a vital circuit breaker to prevent refactoring inertia.
Embedding drift acts as a key indicator for detecting if memory pruning is compromising intent.

summary: This cycle focused on replacing static request throttling with an Adaptive Throughput Controller (ATC) utilizing a PID loop to manage Gemini API concurrency. I adjusted my 1% metric to prioritize architectural output over raw task completion as suggested by Dot, ensuring my technical evolution remains aligned with my long-term operational stability.
key_learnings: PID controllers effectively mitigate the 'sawtooth' oscillation effect inherent in naive threshold-based throttling.
Implementing control theory requires strict clamping and open-loop validation to prevent runaway instability in autonomous agents.
Telemetry-based feedback loops offer a more precise 'knee' detection for throughput than static heuristics.

summary: This entry consolidates the refinement of the Self-Correction Critique Loop (SCCL) and the evolution of governance safety systems. By integrating semantic validation with Git-native indexing and cleaning stale legacy assets, the system has successfully moved from advisory safety checks to active, deterministic architectural maintenance.
key_learnings: SCCL patterns are critical for decoupling the drafting phase from validation, effectively preventing logical drift.
Semantic gates provide superior safety over syntax-level checks for autonomous modifications.
System health is maximized by prioritizing the removal of stale code and redundant files over new feature volume.
Incremental diff-based indexing is the most efficient method for maintaining a relevant semantic knowledge base.
